title: Water Watch Center says it is giving water utilities in 26 states free security monitoring
date_note: Cybersecurity Dive (23 Nov) says the group announced it on Friday, which is 21 November.
org: Water Watch Center (National Rural Water Association and DEF CON Franklin)
summary: Cybersecurity Dive reports that the Water Watch Center, a joint effort of the National Rural Water Association and DEF CON Franklin, says it is providing free security monitoring and assistance to water utilities in 26 states so far. The center pays technology and cybersecurity firms for the intrusion detection services and consultations. The group said nearly 100 utilities have contacted it.
plain: A water-sector group says it is giving free cybersecurity monitoring and help to water utilities in 26 states.
exec: Free monitoring is on offer to US water utilities, a sector the report says Iran-linked hackers breached over the summer.
impact: Free intrusion detection and defensive consultations for participating utilities.

evidence.quote: providing free security monitoring and assistance to water utilities in 26 states so far
Nearly 100 utilities have contacted the center to inquire about its services, the group said.
